song.title: The Day I Tried To Live

guitar.notes: Corrected: Kim Thayil is Soundgarden's guitarist; Chris Cornell was primarily vocalist (occasionally rhythm guitar) so listing him as co-equal guitarist overstates his role. Kim Thayil's Guild S-100 is reasonably well documented.

tone.target: dark grunge crunch with fuzzy sustain and dry mids
tone.profile: dark grunge crunch with fuzzy sustain and dry mids
tone.summary: Fuzz -> OD Boost -> Amp Distortion -> Cab -> EQ -> Chorus (optional) -> Delay.

rig.name: Soundgarden - The Day I Tried To Live - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and stray noise inherent in grunge tones.
Provide initial grit and boost the signal into the fuzz stage.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used here as a versatile, slightly dirty pre-amp to complement the heavy fuzz without sounding too clean.

alternatives.reason: A good alternative for general grit.

blocks.purpose: Achieve the required fuzzy saturation and thick sustain characteristic of grunge.

alternatives.reason: If a more aggressive, biting fuzz is desired.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the Marshall/Hiwatt-style punch and thick low-mid weight.
blocks.gap: The UK 50 provides a classic, powerful British tone suitable for grunge aggression.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic British 4x12 cabinet sound required for the genre.
Enhance the low-mid weight and maintain a dry, focused tone.
blocks.gap: Used to specifically boost the crucial mid-range frequencies that define grunge thickness.

blocks.purpose: Optional subtle movement to add dimension without sounding clean or shimmering.
blocks.gap: The Chorus is kept optional and dialed back, as per the 'avoid chorus/flanger' rule, but can add useful width.

blocks.purpose: Minimal ambience to add depth without sounding wet or big.
blocks.gap: Used only for subtle rhythmic echo, avoiding the 'big reverb' trap.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism for better low-mid definition.

proposals.reason: Enhance the thick, dark grunge tone and mid-weight definition.
